Official title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
Requirement (teletherapy context): Lawfulness, fairness, transparency; purpose limitation; minimisation; accuracy; storage limitation; integrity and confidentiality. Session transcripts and affect data are the minimisation pressure point.

Official title: Principles relating to processing of personal data (accountability)
Requirement (teletherapy context): Demonstrate compliance, not merely achieve it. Every requirement needs an artefact.
Art. 6 basis per purpose. 6(1)(b) contract for service delivery; 6(1)(f) legitimate interests for security/analytics with an LIA. 6(1)(f) cannot carry health data alone.

Official title: Processing of special categories of personal data
Requirement (teletherapy context): Mental-health content, diagnoses, affect inferences and the fact of being a therapy user are special-category data. Default prohibition.

Official title: Processing of special categories of personal data
Requirement (teletherapy context): Preferred condition where care is delivered by or under responsibility of a health professional: medical diagnosis, provision of health care or treatment.

Official title: Processing of special categories of personal data
Requirement (teletherapy context): 9(2)(h) conditional on processing by or under responsibility of a professional bound by professional secrecy. Governs engineering and support access.

Official title: Processing of special categories of personal data
Requirement (teletherapy context): Explicit consent as fallback where 9(2)(h) unavailable (no clinician in the loop, secondary use, research). Separable and withdrawable.
Demonstrable, freely given, as easy to withdraw as to give. Consent bundled into ToS acceptance fails.

Official title: Conditions applicable to child's consent in relation to information society services
Requirement (teletherapy context): Digital consent age 16, lowered to as far as 13 by Member State law. Per-market age gating and verifiable parental authorisation for adolescent therapy.

Official title: Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject
Requirement (teletherapy context): Plain language; one-month response to rights requests. Reading level matters for a distressed user base.

Official title: Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject
Requirement (teletherapy context): Full notice at collection including 13(2)(f) meaningful information about the logic of automated decision-making.

Official title: Information to be provided where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject
Requirement (teletherapy context): Applies to referral data from clinicians, insurers or employers.

Official title: Right of access by the data subject
Requirement (teletherapy context): Access to record including transcripts and model-derived inferences. Decide whether clinician process notes are in scope; national health-record law modifies this.
Correction of clinical record entries subject to health-record integrity rules.

Official title: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
Requirement (teletherapy context): Constrained by 17(3)(b)/(c) health-record retention duties under national law. Do not build or promise an unqualified delete button.
Suspend processing pending accuracy or objection disputes.
Structured, machine-readable export of user-provided and observed data. Continuity-of-care driver.
Absolute for direct marketing; qualified for legitimate-interest processing.
Engages if AI alone sets care pathway, risk tier or access. 22(4) permits special-category ADM only on 9(2)(a) or 9(2)(g) with safeguards. Human review must be meaningful.
Implement and review appropriate technical and organisational measures.

Official title: Data protection by design and by default
Requirement (teletherapy context): Pseudonymisation and minimisation by default; default-off optional affect analytics; no dark patterns in consent flow.
Common where therapists practise independently on the platform. Transparent arrangement plus published essence.

Official title: Representatives of controllers or processors not established in the Union
Requirement (teletherapy context): Non-EU providers targeting EU users must appoint an EU representative.
Art. 28(3) terms with every processor: cloud, transcription, LLM API, analytics, crisis-line integrations. Documented sub-processor chain.
ROPA mandatory. The Art. 30(5) small-organisation exemption does not apply because special categories are processed.
Encryption in transit and at rest, pseudonymisation, resilience, restore capability, regular testing. Recordings and transcripts are the crown jewels.

Official title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
Requirement (teletherapy context): 72 hours from awareness. Mental-health data will rarely clear the 'unlikely to result in a risk' bar.

Official title: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
Requirement (teletherapy context): Without undue delay where high risk. Assume high risk by default for this data class.
Mandatory. 35(3)(b) large-scale special categories is met on its own; 35(3)(a) profiling likely met too. Before launch.
Consult the supervisory authority where high residual risk remains. Adds calendar time.

Official title: Designation of the data protection officer
Requirement (teletherapy context): Mandatory under 37(1)(c): core activities are large-scale special-category processing.
General principle for any third-country transfer.
SCCs plus transfer impact assessment for US-hosted LLM inference, transcription or support tooling.
Narrow and non-repetitive. Do not build routine transfers on 49(1)(a) explicit consent.

Official title: (safeguards for archiving, research and statistics) - title unverified
Requirement (teletherapy context): Engages for secondary use of clinical data in model training or research.

Official title: (general conditions for imposing administrative fines) - title unverified
Requirement (teletherapy context): Up to EUR 20m or 4% worldwide turnover for Art. 5, 6, 7, 9 and rights breaches.
Establish role: provider, deployer or both. Art. 3(14) 'safety component' narrowed by the 2026 amendment.
Sufficient AI literacy for staff. Softened by the 2026 amendment to a measures-based duty; still targets clinicians supervising AI output.

Official title: (processing of special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction) - new
Requirement (teletherapy context): Inserted by Reg. 2026/1744. Permits special-category processing strictly necessary for bias detection and correction under safeguards. Reconcile with Art. 10(5).
No subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques materially distorting behaviour and causing significant harm.

No exploitation of vulnerabilities due to age, disability or specific social or economic situation. Highest-severity row for this product category: review engagement loops, streaks, loss-framing, upsell timing.
Emotion inference prohibited in workplace and education only. A B2B employer or university channel can turn a high-risk feature into a prohibited one.
Inserted by Reg. 2026/1744: non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM generation. Relevant only if a generative avatar or image capability ships.

Official title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): Run the classification. 6(1) product route; 6(2) Annex III route; 6(1a)-(1c) narrow 'safety component'; 6(3) derogation unavailable where profiling occurs.

Official title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): If an Annex III system is assessed as not high-risk, document the assessment before market and still register under Art. 49(2).
Watch item: the Commission may extend Annex III.
Umbrella obligation for the Section 2 requirements.
Continuous lifecycle risk management including foreseeable misuse: crisis-state misuse, dependency, off-label clinical reliance.
Training/validation/test data governance, representativeness, bias examination. 10(5) permits special-category processing for bias detection. Demographic and linguistic coverage is the live risk.
Annex IV technical documentation, complete before market and kept current.
Automatic logging over the lifetime. Design the log schema against GDPR minimisation now; the two obligations pull in opposite directions.

Official title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
Requirement (teletherapy context): Instructions for use enabling deployers to interpret output. Where clinicians deploy, this is the clinical-use-instructions artefact.
Effective oversight by a natural person: interpret, override, disregard. For crisis detection this is a staffed clinical escalation path.
Declared accuracy metrics, resilience, resistance to adversarial manipulation including prompt injection.

Official title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): Consolidated provider duty list.
QMS; integrate with ISO 13485 where also an MDR manufacturer.
Retain documentation 10 years after placing on market.
Retain logs under provider control at least six months unless other law requires longer.

Official title: Corrective actions and duty of information
Requirement (teletherapy context): Withdraw or recall and inform the chain on non-conformity.

Official title: Authorised representatives of providers of high-risk AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): Non-EU providers appoint an EU authorised representative. Distinct from the GDPR Art. 27 representative; you likely need both.

Official title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
Requirement (teletherapy context): Substantially modifying, or putting your name on, a third-party model can make you the provider. Most commonly missed row for teams building on a foundation-model API.

Official title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): Where clinicians or clinics deploy: use per instructions, competent human oversight, monitoring, log retention, inform affected persons.

Official title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): FRIA falls on deployers that are public bodies or private entities providing public services, and Annex III 5(b)/(c) deployers. Engages via public health system contracts. Not general.
Internal control (Annex VI) or notified body (Annex VII). Medical-device route runs through the MDR notified body.
Draw up and keep 10 years.
Affix CE marking.
Register in the EU database before market, including under 49(2) systems assessed as non-high-risk under Art. 6(3).

Official title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): Disclose that the user is interacting with an AI system unless obvious. Applies to any conversational agent regardless of risk tier. 'Obvious' is a weak defence in a therapy context.

Official title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): Mark synthetic audio/image/video/text machine-readably. Engages for synthetic voice or avatar therapists. Pre-2 Aug 2026 systems have until 2 Dec 2026.

Official title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): Disclosure clear and distinguishable at the latest at first interaction, and accessible. Not buried in settings or ToS.

Official title: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan for high-risk AI systems
Requirement (teletherapy context): Post-market monitoring plan; integrate with MDR post-market surveillance where both apply.
Report serious incidents to market surveillance authorities. Define to include missed crisis detection and harmful output; align the clock with GDPR Art. 33.

Official title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
Requirement (teletherapy context): Affected persons may obtain a clear and meaningful explanation of the AI system's role in decisions with legal or similarly significant effects. Overlaps GDPR Art. 22; build one capability.
Up to EUR 35m or 7% worldwide turnover for Art. 5 prohibitions; up to EUR 15m or 3% for most other obligations.
Amended by Reg. 2026/1744: Annex III high-risk 2 Dec 2027; Annex I / Art. 6(1) high-risk 2 Aug 2028.
